questions.question: According to the article, what was the outcome of the Battle of Kadesh for Ramesses II?
options: It was generally considered a stalemate.
It was a decisive Egyptian victory.
It was a decisive Hittite victory.
It was an indecisive skirmish with no casualties.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Ramesses conducted no fewer than 15 military campaigns, all resulting in victories, excluding the Battle of Kadesh, which is generally considered a stalemate.
Incorrect. Although Ramesses claimed a great victory, the article excludes Kadesh from his victories and describes it as generally considered a stalemate.
Incorrect. The article does not characterize Kadesh as a decisive Hittite victory; it calls it a stalemate.
Incorrect. The article describes a major battle with ambushes, chariotry, and routs, not an indecisive skirmish with no casualties.

questions.question: How many Sed festivals did Ramesses II celebrate?
options: Thirteen or fourteen
Six
Twenty-one
Sixty-six
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that he celebrated an unprecedented thirteen or fourteen Sed festivalsâmore than any other pharaoh.
Incorrect. Six is not mentioned in connection with Sed festivals in the article.
Incorrect. Twenty-one refers to the year of his reign when he concluded the peace treaty with the Hittites, not Sed festivals.
Incorrect. Sixty-six refers to the length of his reign in years, not the number of Sed festivals.

questions.question: Where is Ramesses II's mummy currently on display?
options: National Museum of Egyptian Civilization in Cairo
Valley of the Kings
Royal Cache
Pi-Ramesses
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Ramesses' mummy is now on display at the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization, located in Cairo.
Incorrect. The Valley of the Kings is where he was originally buried in tomb KV7, not where his mummy is displayed today.
Incorrect. The Royal Cache is where his body was later moved and discovered in 1881, not its current display location.
Incorrect. Pi-Ramesses was the city he established as Egypt's new capital, not a museum location.

questions.question: What did Ramesses II construct at Pi-Ramesses to support his Syrian campaigns?
options: Factories to manufacture weapons, chariots, and shields
A temple dedicated to the god Amun
A naval fleet to patrol the Nile Delta
A tomb for his burial in the Valley of the Kings
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that at Pi-Ramesses he built factories to manufacture weapons, chariots, and shields, supposedly producing some 1,000 weapons in a week, about 250 chariots in two weeks, and 1,000 shields in a week and a half.
Incorrect. The article does not mention constructing a temple dedicated to Amun at Pi-Ramesses.
Incorrect. The article does not mention building a naval fleet at Pi-Ramesses to patrol the Nile Delta.
Incorrect. His tomb KV7 is in the Valley of the Kings, not at Pi-Ramesses.

questions.question: In which regnal year did Ramesses II conclude the Treaty of Kadesh with the Hittites?
options: Year 21
Year 5
Year 10
Year 67
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that eventually, in the twenty-first year of his reign (1259 BC), Ramesses concluded an agreement at Kadesh to end the conflict.
Incorrect. Year 5 was when the Battle of Kadesh took place, not when the treaty was concluded.
Incorrect. Year 10 was when Ramesses marched against Dapur once more, not when the treaty was concluded.
Incorrect. Year 67 relates to the end of his reign and his death, not the treaty.

questions.question: According to the article, what is the most likely age of Ramesses II at death?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that estimates of his age at death vary, although 90 or 91 is considered to be the most likely figure.
Incorrect. 25 is the age at which he ascended to the throne, not his age at death.
Incorrect. 66 is the length of his reign in years, not his age at death.
Incorrect. 11 is approximately Ramesses II's age when his grandfather Ramesses I was appointed successor by Horemheb, not his age at death.

questions.question: What does the article say about Ramesses II's association with the pharaoh of the Exodus?
options: Scholars dispute this association.
It is confirmed by contemporary Egyptian records.
It is supported by the Jewish historian Josephus.
It is accepted by Mostafa Wazir and Lester L. Grabbe.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that scholars dispute Ramesses II's association with the popular depiction of him as the pharaoh of the Exodus, including Mostafa Wazir and Lester L. Grabbe.
Incorrect. The article does not say contemporary Egyptian records confirm this association; rather, scholars dispute it.
Incorrect. Josephus is mentioned in connection with assigning Ramesses II a reign of 66 years, 2 months, not with supporting the Exodus association.
Incorrect. Mostafa Wazir and Lester L. Grabbe are cited as scholars who dispute the association, not support it.

questions.question: What happened to Ramesses II's body after his initial burial in KV7?
options: It was moved to the Royal Cache, where it was discovered in 1881.
It was left undisturbed in KV7 until modern times.
It was cremated and scattered in the Nile Delta.
It was transferred to Pi-Ramesses as a new capital monument.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that upon his death he was buried in KV7 in the Valley of the Kings; his body was later moved to the Royal Cache, where it was discovered by archaeologists in 1881.
Incorrect. The article explicitly states his body was later moved from KV7 to the Royal Cache.
Incorrect. The article does not mention cremation or scattering ashes in the Nile Delta.
Incorrect. Pi-Ramesses was his capital city, not a destination for his mummified body.
